I've thrown this question elsewhere on Voat before, and didn't quite get the response I wanted. The question makes me sound clueless and naive, but I'd rather admit to those qualities than remain ignorant. Also related question: What's a good way to learn to investigate things?
I feel the need to improve my Critical Thinking, what is the best way for me to (re)learn it?

The way to improve critical thinking is simple. Learn as many logical fallacies as you can, and practice identifying them.

Start here; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_fallacies

Also the inverse, learn valid syllogisms and how to identify them.

Start here: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_valid_argument_forms

Notice the first list is MUCH longer than the second - there are more ways to be wrong than right.

It's interesting that you say that you feel clueless and naive for asking a question.

It is as if asking a question shows a lack of knowing which is seen as weakness in our current culture. Like you're a 'loser' to the group, and you can't be a 'winner' if you don't know shit - but if you don't know shit we ain't going to teach you shit either. When people jump on us for wishing to further our understanding then either they are reacting out of fear of their own ignorance or because they feel an entitlement to protect their hard-earned academic knowledge from the layperson.

Therefore, in this kind of societal atmosphere, admitting that we don't know something is really more a sign of strength than anything else and asking questions is one of the best ways to start (re)training the critically-minded part of your person.

A few examples; Why is a person/institution arguing a point? What/who benefits from you believing the argument? Where does the argument originate from? And of course, always follow the money.

Research the concept of 'bias'. Learn the common cognitive biases that people tend to have and then reflect on how these have affected you in your life (I've linked an article here but this is just a few examples, there are plenty of other biases).

Also, always remember that the key to critical thinking is skepticism. Learn to fact check things, especially things you see online (if for no other reason than they are so easy to fact check thus it makes for good practice) rather than simply accepting them - which people will tend to do when the statement is something that the person wants to believe. I forget what that bias is called but it's more important to understand the concepts than the naming ;)
